meta.title: Screen Recorder (QA mode) | Pedro Morago
meta.description: A Chrome extension I built for bug reports. It records console logs and network requests with the video, and each step with a Cypress or Playwright selector.
meta.shareDescription: A Chrome extension for bug reports that records console logs, network requests and your steps with the video. I test it against a page that breaks on demand.

title: Screen Recorder (QA mode)
lede: A Chrome extension that records a bug together with what a developer needs to reproduce it. I built it for my own bug reports, and anyone can install it in about 30 seconds.

facts.label: Type
facts.text: Chrome extension (Manifest V3), published on GitHub

facts.label: Tech
facts.text: JavaScript, chrome.desktopCapture, Cypress, Playwright, GitHub Actions

facts.label: Tested against
facts.text: [A bug bench I built for it ↗](https://bench.pedromorago.com/)

blocks.text: I used a tool called Nimbus to record bugs for my reports. When it changed, I rebuilt the features I relied on in my own extension, and then added the ones I wanted.

items: Console logs and network requests recorded along with the video. No tool I had did that for me.
Test steps with Playwright selectors, so I don't have to repeat a test just to write its steps down.
Marking bugs on the video, which helps a lot with frontend issues.
Exporting only the audio, for example from a meeting.

sections.title: What you get from one recording

items: A recording of your screen, a window or a single tab, with no time limit, no watermark and no account.
Console logs synced to the video, including uncaught exceptions.
Network requests, exported as a HAR file.
Numbered steps, recorded automatically from clicks, forms and page changes, including navigation inside single-page apps. Typed values are never logged.
A `*.steps.md` export in which each step has a paste-ready Cypress or Playwright selector, so the list can become the skeleton of a regression test.
Annotations drawn on the video while you record, and markers added with a keyboard shortcut.
The full report, filed directly as an issue in Jira Cloud or Linear.

blocks.text: I didn't want to check the recorder against whatever a real website happened to do that day. So I built a bug bench for it, a page that breaks on demand. It can return a 500 on a write, throw an uncaught exception, or send a response that says OK and means the opposite. Each failure is known in advance, so I can check the recording against it.

items: Download the zip from the latest release and unzip it.
Open `chrome://extensions` and turn on Developer mode.
Choose Load unpacked and select the unzipped folder.

blocks.text: No store account and no build step.
